item.text:
**6B.1 Assessment**
Mostly no. There is real evidence of welfare-oriented activity in health, disaster response, social protection, and Rohingya support, but much of it is partner-led, targeted, or technocratic. The dominant 2024 pattern still looks like regime preservation and coercive control taking precedence over human welfare as a core purpose.

**Accepted Claims**
- **[World Bank Helps Bangladesh Provide Basic Services, Opportunities, and Build Resilience for Displaced Rohingya and Host Communities](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/05/28/world-bank-helps-bangladesh-provide-basic-services-opportunities-and-build-resilience-for-displaced-rohingya-and-host-co)** | World Bank | May 28, 2024 | Claim: Bangladesh, with World Bank support, funded health, nutrition, education, water, shelters, livelihood support, and GBV prevention for Rohingya and host communities. This is the strongest positive evidence that welfare was treated as a real policy object, though it is still largely externally financed and crisis-specific. | QIDs: 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.10

- **[UNFPA Bangladesh Annual Report 2024](https://bangladesh.unfpa.org/en/unfpa-bangladesh-annual-report-2024)** | UNFPA Bangladesh | 2024 | Claim: UNFPA delivered targeted services to women, girls, indigenous communities, transgender people, sex workers, and disaster-affected districts, including emergency reproductive health and cash assistance. This shows concrete concern for vulnerable people, but it is humanitarian service delivery rather than strong proof that Hasina made welfare the core purpose of rule. | QIDs: 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **[Advancing Healthcare Excellence: WHO's Role in Developing the First National Medical Education Strategy in Bangladesh!](https://www.who.int/bangladesh/news/detail/04-03-2024-advancing-healthcare-excellence-who-s-role-in-developing-the-first-national-medical-education-strategy-in-bangladesh)** | WHO Bangladesh | March 4, 2024 | Claim: the Ministry of Health, with WHO support, launched Bangladesh’s first national medical education strategy to improve curriculum, accreditation, faculty development, and digital transformation. This is a real pro-welfare governance signal because it addresses health-system quality, not just visibility or patronage. | QIDs: 6B.1, 5B.9, 5B.10

- **[Bangladesh - Cash Transfer Modernization Project: Improving Transparency and Efficiency of Safety Nets](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099739201032424234)** | World Bank | January 1, 2024 | Claim: Bangladesh already had cash-transfer programs aimed at the poorest and most socially excluded, including widows, older people, and disabled people. This is limited positive background evidence for welfare orientation, but it also shows the need for modernization because coverage and delivery were still incomplete. | QIDs: 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.10

- **[Bangladesh: Repression, Security Force Abuses Discredit Elections](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/bangladesh-repression-security-force-abuses-discredit-elections)** | Human Rights Watch | January 11, 2024 | Claim: authorities arrested critics, suppressed dissent, and used violence against opposition members ahead of the election. This is strong counterevidence: a ruler treating control and intimidation as more important than the welfare of citizens’ rights and safety. | QIDs: 6B.1, 3B.3, 5B.1

- **[Bangladesh: Türk decries government crackdown, urges respect for international human rights standards](https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights)** | United Nations / OHCHR | July 26, 2024 | Claim: more than 170 people were reported killed, some injured people were denied medical care, and the UN said there was no effort to protect people from attacks by groups affiliated with the government. This is very strong evidence that welfare and civilian protection were not the governing priority during the July crisis. | QIDs: 6B.1, 3B.3, 5B.7, 5B.9

- **[Bangladesh: Freedom in the World 2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-world/2024)** | Freedom House | 2024 | Claim: the Awami League consolidated power through harassment of the opposition and critical media; corruption was endemic; and minorities and refugees, especially Rohingya, faced discrimination and insecure access to services. This supports the view that the regime’s operating logic was partisan control, not neutral welfare maximization. | QIDs: 6B.1, 5B.5, 5B.8, 5B.10

- **[Macro Poverty Outlook for Bangladesh: October 2024](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099659510152422672)** | World Bank | October 1, 2024 | Claim: growth was expected to slow, extreme poverty was projected to rise, and inequality was projected to increase by more than one Gini point, with jobs still weak. This is strong evidence that 2024 did not leave welfare on a clearly better trajectory for ordinary people. | QIDs: 6B.1, 5B.9, 5B.10, 5B.8

**Search Gap**
- The strongest positive evidence is narrow and often partner-led: health systems, humanitarian aid, targeted safety nets, and Rohingya support.
- I did not find strong 2024 evidence that Hasina’s own governing style treated human welfare as the overriding purpose across the whole state. The counterevidence is broader and more direct: repression, censorship, violent crisis response, and worsening poverty/inequality.
